sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: a same-metric figure with two scopes inside one paper (Doc 5's R² before and after it fine-tunes on its own 39 test cells), joined to the one held-out-cell R² another paper prints (Doc 6); medium (high acceptable); quick test survived (user chat 2026-10-14: "i05, i01, i02 survived"); difficulty result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 6 l215 (trained on the first four Batch1 batteries, tested on the rest; average R² 0.977) -> GAT-BiGRU's unseen-cell score. Doc 5 l186 and l389 (fine-tuning on the test set, the target domain) with l212 and Table 4 (R² 0.959 before, 0.977 after, over 39 batteries) -> the unseen-cell score is 0.959. 0.977 - 0.959 = 0.018.
- Universe: not applicable (one value). Every R² either paper prints, searched on 2026-10-14: Doc 6 prints one, 0.977 (l215; its main results, a random 6:4 split within every cell at l169, print no R², and its Tables 1-11 are not in the text). Doc 5 prints 0.97 (summary, l7, after transfer), 0.959 and 0.977 (Table 4 l195, Results l212, Methods l393, Table 5 scheme 1 l226), 0.986 and 0.998 (the transfer paragraph l188, which cites Table 4 but contradicts it), and the other schemes, SOC windows, sampling intervals and ablations (Tables 5-7, l224-306), all after fine-tuning or on other set-ups.
- Necessity: Doc 6 is the only source of the GAT-BiGRU's held-out-cell R² (no other paper reports that model); with Doc 6 deleted the minuend is unknowable. Doc 5 is the only source of the CNN–self-attention model's scores and of the fact that its test cells were used for fine-tuning; with Doc 5 deleted the subtrahend is unknowable. Closed book: no route (the platform's closed-book solver has no 2025 results for either model).
- Selected-lever checks: the scope trap recomputed: after-fine-tuning 0.977 gives 0.000; the transfer paragraph's after value 0.998 gives -0.021 and its before value 0.986 gives -0.009; the summary's 0.97 gives 0.007. Only the before-fine-tuning 0.959, printed in Table 4, the Results and the Methods, is on cells the model never saw.
- Targeted failure modes: Look-alike measure / Takes the wrong line item: 0.000 (Doc 5's after-transfer 0.977, Table 4's second column, taken for the unseen-cell score). Considered and not declared, predicted only: the transfer paragraph's contradictory figures (-0.009 or -0.021). No measured attempts yet (the quick test returned no panel).
- Calculation verification: 0.977 - 0.959 = 0.018, exact at three decimals (script, 2026-10-14).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no passage states either model's score on unseen cells as such, and none compares the two papers. The bundle overview prints Doc 5's "0.97 R2" (after transfer) and no Doc 6 R². A search for "R2" in Doc 5 lands on the transfer paragraph (l188) two lines below the fine-tuning sentence (l186). Shortest complete route: Doc 6 l215, Doc 5 l186 and l212.
- Precision/readings: Doc 5's after-transfer 0.977 gives 0.000 and is rejected by "never saw": those 39 cells were the fine-tuning data (l186, l389). The transfer paragraph's 0.986/0.998 contradict the Table 4 the paragraph cites and the Results and Methods, and the after value is post-fine-tuning anyway. "The fast-charging model" read as the final, fine-tuned network only, so that no unseen-cell score exists: the question asks for the model's score on cells it never saw, and Doc 5 reports that network's score on those cells before it saw them (0.959); a reviewer could still raise this, so read the form's "One defensible answer" check before a run. Doc 6's "four batteries" are training cells; its 0.977 is over the remaining Batch1 cells, the only R² it prints.
- Completeness: capture complete; Doc 6's tables are absent from the platform text itself, so its main-result R² values are not readable by anyone, and the held-out-cell paragraph (l215) is.
- Style/set review: q01 uses Doc 1 and Doc 7 only; no shared passage. Sketch i04 (untested) also turns on Doc 6's held-out versus within-cell results; it is not written up.
- Warnings answered: see the hand-over.
sections.question: On cells each model never saw, what is the GAT-BiGRU SOH model's average R² minus the fast-charging CNN–self-attention model's, to three decimal places?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 6, the section on the model's generalization performance): the GAT-BiGRU model was trained on data from the first four Batch1 batteries and tested on the remaining batteries of that batch; on those batteries its average R² was 0.977.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 5, the transfer learning section): after loading the pre-trained weights, the authors fine-tuned the CNN-self-attention model on data from the test set, its target domain.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 5, results of health estimation and Table 4): across its test batteries the model's average R² was 0.959 before transfer learning and 0.977 after it.

Step 4. Reading (Doc 5): the after-transfer score comes from the same test batteries the model had just been fine-tuned on (Step 2), so its score on cells it never saw is the before-transfer score.

Step 5. Calculation (Doc 6 and Doc 5): 0.977 - 0.959 = 0.018.

Decoy: Doc 5's after-transfer score, the figure it reports most often, would give no difference at all.

Step 6. Final answer (Doc 6 and Doc 5): 0.018.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Look-alike measure
How a careless solver fails: Takes the wrong line item

Why these are traps: Look-alike measure: Doc 5 gives R² 0.959 before and 0.977 after fine-tuning on its 39 test cells (Results; Table 4). Taking the after-fine-tuning figure gives 0.977 - 0.977 = 0.000. Those cells were unseen only before fine-tuning, so the gold uses 0.959: 0.018.
